title: Beyond the Prompt: Jailbreaking Function-Calling LLMs via Simulated Moderation Traces
abstract: arXiv:2607.00481v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Jailbreak attacks remain a critical threat to the safe deployment of large language models (LLMs). While prior work has primarily studied attacks and defenses at the prompt level, we show that this prompt-centric paradigm overlooks a structural vulnerability in stateful, function-calling environments. In such applications, developer-defined schemas, structured arguments, and untrusted tool outputs are interleaved into a single shared model context. This architecture expands the attack surface by blurring the boundary between trusted control logic and untrusted data, allowing adversarial intent to be distributed across a multi-turn execution path. We exploit this architectural flaw through SMT, a black-box attack framework based on Simulated Moderation Traces. translated_title: 超越提示词：通过模拟审核轨迹越狱函数调用大语言模型
translated_abstract: 越狱攻击仍然是大语言模型（LLM）安全部署的重大威胁。虽然先前的工作主要在提示词层面研究攻击与防御，但我们表明这种以提示词为中心的范式忽略了有状态的函数调用环境中的一个结构性漏洞。在这类应用中，开发者定义的模式、结构化参数和不可信的工具输出被交错混合到单一的共享模型上下文中。这种架构通过模糊可信控制逻辑与不可信数据之间的边界来扩大攻击面，使对抗意图能够分布在多轮执行路径中。我们通过SMT——一种基于模拟审核轨迹的黑盒攻击框架——利用这一架构缺陷。SMT摒弃了纯提示词交互方式，构建了一个模拟合法审核审计工作流的多轮轨迹。在该轨迹中，一个……
tldr: 本文提出SMT黑盒攻击框架，通过构建模拟合法审核审计工作流的多轮轨迹，利用函数调用环境中可信控制逻辑与不可信数据边界模糊的结构性漏洞，成功越狱函数调用大语言模型。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SMT, a black-box attack framework that jailbreaks function-calling LLMs by exploiting structural vulnerabilities where trusted control logic and untrusted data are blurred, using simulated multi-turn trajectories of legitimate moderation-auditing workflows.
